title: 1982 AHSME Problem 15
statement: Let \(\lfloor z\rfloor\) denote the greatest integer not exceeding \(z.\) Let \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy the simultaneous equations \[ \begin{aligned} y&=2\lfloor x\rfloor+3,\\ y&=3\lfloor x-2\rfloor+5. \end{aligned} \] If \(x\) is not an integer, then \(x+y\) is

solutions.text:
For nonintegral \(x,\) let \(n=\lfloor x\rfloor;\) then \(\lfloor x-2\rfloor=n-2.\) Thus \(2n+3=3(n-2)+5,\) so \(n=4\) and \(y=11.\) Since \(4\lt x\lt5,\) we have \(15\lt x+y\lt16.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: For nonintegral \(x,\) relate \(\lfloor x-2\rfloor\) to \(\lfloor x\rfloor\)
Let \(n=\lfloor x\rfloor\) and equate the two formulas for \(y\)
